- ₹300 Cr preferential issue completed during Q1 FY27 at ₹502/share, anchored by WhiteOak, Kotak, 360 ONE and ValueQuest.
- ₹225 Cr of the proceeds earmarked for debt repayment, "strengthening balance sheet and lowering finance cost outgo"; management expects it to "materially reduce leverage and finance costs, improve return ratios".
- The additional pellet capacity "is proposed to be housed under the InVIT, enabling efficient capital deployment".

- Deleveraging is listed as a Vision 2030 operating-efficiency lever, but the slide's own wording is internally inconsistent: "Debt reduction <2x → ~3.5x by FY30".
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Scale: described as one of India's largest process piping players by installed capacity and among the leading players globally, built over nearly four decades since incorporation in 1988.
- Qualification barrier: supplier approvals from NTPC for super-critical piping and NPCIL for nuclear applications, plus a certification stack spanning ISO 9001:2015, ISO 3834-2, ISO 14001, ISO 45001, PED/PED Module-H and ASME PP, S, U and U2 stamps.
- Backward integration: the captive Seamless Pipe Manufacturing Plant commissioned at Anjar in March 2026 reduces dependence on external suppliers and already carries NTPC approval, foreign-OEM qualification and its first commercial order.
- Repeat-business franchise: a marquee multi-continent customer base including Reliance, ADNOC, Tata Projects, HMEL, Technip Energies, JGC, McDermott, John Cockerill, GE Vernova, Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, Siemens, Doosan, BHEL and L&T, with a stated track record of consistent, repeat business.
- Shift to structural customer lock-in: a Reservation Agreement with an international EPC major for a majority of DEE's HRSG pipe spool fabrication capacity plus a multi-million-dollar Letter of Intent from a global OEM, described as a move from tender-driven business to capacity-reservation partnerships.
- Logistics and sourcing position at Anjar: proximity to Kandla and Mundra ports cuts transit time both ways, and the western-India location sits near numerous pipe mills and plate manufacturers, allowing raw material delivery within 1-2 days of readiness.
- Automation and process capability: robotic and automated welding (KUKA, ABB, Fanuc, Lincoln, Migatronic), induction bending, conventional and digital radiography, post-weld heat treatment and clean-room manufacturing.
- Turnkey engineering: engineering, design, fabrication and installation delivered end-to-end through a dedicated Chennai Engineering Division rather than as componentised scopes.
- Footprint: seven manufacturing facilities across India and Thailand plus the Chennai engineering division, with total welding capacity in excess of 17,000 inch-diameter per day.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Raw material price volatility in steel and specialised alloys — Named first among the Company's principal risks in the MD&A Risks and Concerns section: volatility in raw material prices for steel and specialised alloys can pressure production costs and margins. For a build-to-print fabricator executing fixed-scope project orders this feeds straight through to gross margin.
- Execution risk on the pace of utilisation ramp-up at the newly commissioned Anjar and seamless pipe capacity — The MD&A states explicitly that FY26's capacity additions carry execution risk on the pace of utilisation ramp-up at Anjar and the seamless pipe plant. This is the central structural risk of the current phase: the FY27 margin and revenue case rests on operating leverage from capacity that is commissioned but not yet utilised, so a slower ramp turns fixed cost and depreciation into margin drag rather than expansion. Management says it is actively addressing this through the FY27 utilisation programme.
- Elevated working capital cycle following capex-driven inventory build-out — The MD&A states the Company's working capital cycle remains elevated following capex-driven inventory build-out, to be addressed through an FY27 working-capital normalisation programme. In a project-execution business an elevated cycle ties up cash precisely as the order book grows, and the routed ratio commentary attributes prior-year declines in inventory turnover and net capital turnover to inventory, receivables and fixed-deposit growth.
- Regulatory and compliance requirements across the global markets served — The MD&A cites stringent regulatory and compliance requirements across the global markets DEE serves, non-compliance with which could result in penalties, delays or reputational impact. Because the business depends on maintained supplier approvals and certifications, a lapse risks eligibility to bid, not merely a fine.
- Geopolitical risk, including trade restrictions and tariff actions — Flagged in the MD&A as capable of disrupting supply chains and affecting market access. This is structural for DEE given its export exposure and its dependence on specialised material inputs.
- Sub-judice tariff dispute with Punjab State Power Corporation Limited affecting the biomass power segment — The auditor's report carries an Emphasis of Matter drawing attention to Note 46, which describes the uncertainty relating to PSPCL's appeal before the Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL), New Delhi and the Company's own Civil Writ Petition before the High Court of Punjab and Haryana, concerning PSPCL's retrospective downward revision of tariff effective 1 January 2024. The matters are sub-judice and no adjustments have been made in the standalone financial statements; the auditor's opinion is not modified in respect of the matter. The MD&A separately records that the favourable PSERC order of 27 March 2026 for Malwa Power's Muktsar plant is itself being challenged by PSPCL, so the segment's tariff basis is unsettled in both directions.
- Competitive and technological pressure requiring continuous investment in innovation and capacity — Listed in the MD&A Risks and Concerns paragraph as a principal risk - a standing claim on capital and R&D even after management declares the current build phase substantially complete.
- Macroeconomic exposure to currency and interest-rate movements — Cited among the MD&A's principal risks. The exposure is amplified by leverage carried through the capex phase; the MD&A states the balance-sheet strengthening through the FY26 preferential issue is intended to build additional resilience against these risks.

outlook.body:
- Shift from a multi-year, capex-heavy build phase into an execution and utilisation phase - FY26 completed three capacity milestones (Anjar scaled to 30,000 MTPA, the captive Seamless Pipe Manufacturing Plant commissioned, and the biomass pellet facility set up), and management states capex is now substantially complete with the larger benefit still ahead as utilisation ramps through FY27.
- Backward integration into seamless pipe: the captive Anjar plant reduces dependence on external suppliers and already carries NTPC approval, foreign-OEM qualification and a first order.
- Network re-specialisation: Anjar, close to Kandla and Mundra ports, now carries oil & gas and export execution, freeing the Palwal facility to focus on higher-margin power sector work.
- Move from tender-driven business to structural, capacity-reservation partnerships - evidenced by a Reservation Agreement with an international EPC major for a majority of DEE's HRSG pipe spool fabrication capacity and a multi-million-dollar Letter of Intent from a global OEM.
- Improve order-book quality, not just size: stronger alloy-steel content and job-work mix supporting margins, with further accretion expected as the seamless plant reaches optimal utilisation.
- Build new energy verticals - nuclear (on the back of NPCIL approval), data centres and semiconductor fabs, green hydrogen and industrial gas (via the stake in Molsieve Design Ltd covering nitrogen generation, oxygen plants, ammonia cracking and hydrogen purification), and carbon capture.
- Restructure the non-core power segment toward self-sustainability: the PSERC tariff order for Malwa Power plus commissioning of the Gulabewala biomass pellet plant, together targeting segment cash neutrality in FY27.
- Enter renewable-energy fabrication through the heavy fabrication segment (wind turbine towers via DEE Fabricom India Private Limited), which secured its first windmill tower order with material during FY26.
- Strengthen the balance sheet and deleverage: a Rs 300 crore preferential issue after year-end at Rs 502 per share with the substantial majority of net proceeds earmarked for debt repayment, with no change in control.
- Working-capital normalisation as a stated FY27 priority, alongside utilisation ramp-up and disciplined capex limited to completion and maintenance spends.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: FY26 was the year DEE's multi-year growth capex programme converted into commissioned, revenue-generating capacity, and management states capex is now substantially complete. The Anjar Pipe Fabrication Unit was scaled in stages from 3,000 MTPA in April 2024 to a fully commissioned 30,000 MTPA in September 2025, ahead of the original October 2025 target - a U-shaped, automation-led facility close to Kandla and Mundra ports that now carries the Company's oil & gas and export execution and frees the Palwal facility for higher-margin power sector work. Alongside it, India's first captive Seamless Pipe Manufacturing Plant of its kind was commissioned on the same Anjar site, with commercial production commencing 19 March 2026 at 7,000 MTPA installed capacity and a stated capital investment of approximately Rs 89.74 crore (Rs 63.37 crore plant and machinery, Rs 24.82 crore building, Rs 1.55 crore electrical infrastructure); it already carries NTPC approval, foreign-OEM qualification and a first commercial order of about Rs 58 crore for execution through December 2026. In the non-core power segment, a new 72,000 MTPA biomass pellet plant at Gulabewala, Muktsar was set up during FY26 and commenced commercial operations in Q1 FY27, converting agricultural residue into pellets for co-firing at thermal power plants. The heavy fabrication segment, making wind turbine towers through DEE Fabricom India Private Limited, carries an installed capacity of 32,400 MT/year and secured its first windmill tower order with material during FY26. These projects were funded through a combination of internal accruals and debt; subsequent to year-end the Company raised a Rs 300 crore preferential issue with roughly 75-77% of net proceeds directed toward debt repayment. Looking forward, FY27 targets full/optimal utilisation at the Anjar fabrication facility and 60-70% utilisation at the seamless pipe plant, with incremental revenue contribution expected from Q1 FY27; capex beyond FY27 will be limited to completion and maintenance spends, with any incremental capacity triggered only by sustained anchor-customer commitments.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- A synchronised demand cycle across every market DEE serves - thermal power, refining and exports, an emerging nuclear opportunity backed by NPCIL approval, and new growth verticals in data centres and semiconductor fabs.
- Sustained global build-out of gas-fired and combined-cycle power capacity to meet rising electricity demand, particularly from data centres and AI infrastructure.
- Continued investment in oil & gas and petrochemical capacity, especially across the Middle East and North America.
- An accelerating energy-transition and decarbonisation agenda spanning green hydrogen, carbon capture and grid-scale renewables.
- Order backlogs at major OEMs and EPCs - DEE's principal customer base - at or near multi-year highs.
- United States: energy and industrial policy favouring domestic manufacturing, LNG export capacity and gas-fired power generation to meet data-centre-driven electricity demand; sustained backlogs at OEMs such as GE Vernova.
- Middle East: GCC diversification investment under programmes such as Saudi Vision 2030, Iraq's refinery upgrade and reconstruction programme, and the UAE's expanding industrial base, reinforced by DEE's ADNOC relationship.
- Southeast Asia: Thailand's role as a regional manufacturing and export hub, power-sector capacity additions in Vietnam and Taiwan's semiconductor and power infrastructure investment supporting order inflows from the Thailand entity.
- Europe: energy security and industrial decarbonisation sustaining investment in gas-based power and re-gasification infrastructure, with relationships at MAN Energy Solutions and John Cockerill.
- India: fiscal focus on capital expenditure, an expanding thermal and nuclear power capacity pipeline, ongoing refining-capacity expansion, and emerging opportunities in green hydrogen, data centres and semiconductor manufacturing underpinning a robust domestic ordering cycle.
- Margin lever: utilisation ramp-up at both the Anjar fabrication facility and the seamless pipe plant is expected to be a primary driver of margin expansion into FY27, through operating leverage on newly commissioned capacity.
- Mix lever: stronger alloy-steel content and a higher job-work mix in the order book supporting margins.
- Structural tailwinds cited: India's capex-led infrastructure cycle, the Union Budget's continued focus on industrial and infrastructure investment, an emerging nuclear capacity programme, and global demand from data centres, gas-turbine backlogs and refining capex.
- Financing lever: the post-year-end preferential issue is expected to reduce finance costs and leverage from FY27.
- Closing order book of Rs 1,940 crore, up 58% year-on-year, with a further Rs 211 crore in L1 positions, described as maintaining strong revenue visibility into FY27.
- FY27 order inflow guidance of more than Rs 2,000 crore, split approximately 60% power and 40% oil & gas, and around 60% domestic with 35-40% export.
- Reservation Agreement with an international EPC major for a majority of DEE's HRSG pipe spool fabrication capacity.
- Multi-million-dollar Letter of Intent from a global OEM.
- First commercial order for the new seamless pipe plant of approximately Rs 58 crore, for execution through December 2026.
- New orders won for the Thailand entity and from the domestic power sector during FY26.
- First windmill tower order with material secured by the heavy fabrication segment during FY26.
- Order book described as having grown in size and quality, with stronger alloy-steel content and job-work mix supporting margins.

deepdive.thesis: Strong Q1FY26 performance driven by 21% revenue growth and 44.7% EBITDA margin expansion, with capacity expansion at Anjar ahead of schedule and strategic entry into green hydrogen via Molsieve acquisition and Clean-Tech partnership creating a new high-margin growth pillar.

open.item: Expect first hydrogen business/bids to convert in 6-9 months; detailed hydrogen revenue projections to be given in the next or next-to-next earnings call.
Around INR25-30 crores capex already done in Q1 FY26; expected total capital cost of around INR100 crores within the financial year to reach planned process piping and seamless piping capacities.

Malwa Power impairment audit qualification expected to be resolved to a clean opinion by the third quarter (of FY27), with no impairment or financial contingency anticipated given upward tariff revision and pellet plant.

Expecting more than INR2,000 crores of order inflow in FY27, with ~60% from the power sector and the rest from oil and gas; 60-65% domestic and 35-40% export (contingent on BHEL orders materialising).
Committed to at least INR1,500 crores revenue in FY27 as a conservative target, with likely upside beyond that given order traction.
Expecting around 65-70% of FY27 revenue from the power sector (thermal from India and HRSG from abroad); power orders currently ~INR1,000-1,200 cr in order book.
Targeting working capital cycle of around 180 days in FY27 (first target, eventually 150 days): inventory days down 15-20 days, debtor days ~95-100, payable days improved to above 70-75.

Malwa Power tariff revised up to Rs. 5.22/KwH from Rs. 3.5/KwH with ~INR5.52 cr retrospective recovery; combined power + biomass pellet revenue expected ~INR47.71 cr in FY27; biomass pellet facility to offset cash burn and stabilise segment.
FY27 capex to be limited to around INR20-30 crores (remaining/maintenance), though a new capacity expansion (e.g. for nuclear) is on the drawing board and could add capex.
Expect Anjar fabrication facility to reach optimal/expected utilisation in FY27 and the seamless plant to ramp to around 60-70%.
Guided consolidated EBITDA margin of above 19% going forward.
Targeting FY27 order book of ~INR2,000 crores funded from improved internal cash flow without new debt (unless a sudden ~INR1,000 crore order block arises).
Going forward in FY27, core business (piping and fabrication) EBITDA margin expected in the 18% to 20% range.
High-wall thickness pipe plant expected to generate around INR200 crores of revenue at full capacity (asset turnover roughly 2x in first fiscal).
Seamless pipe used for backward integration adds to EBITDA via purchase margin; when sold independently as commodity, margin expected around 20%.
Conservative growth estimate of 20% CAGR, with possibility of 25-30% given HRSG/power traction.
Existing facilities (post remaining capex) can generate around INR2,500 crores revenue; target of INR2,500 crores by FY30 (could be earlier with stronger order flow).
Reiterated 3x revenue growth target over 3-5 years (by FY30), driven mainly by the Anjar expansion.
Maintains long-term guidance of a threefold increase in revenue over the next 3 to 5 years.
Reiterated long-term guidance of a threefold increase in revenue in 3 to 5 years.
